blocks.cap: Gin's handwriting, face up after all, the leaning loops of the entries after the 14th

blocks.p: The ink had leaned before the man did. That was what Rei saw first, with the page turned to the lamp. Not a tremor. A lean.

He had saved his brother's clock for last because he knew that once he looked at it he would not be able to look at anything else. Here was Gin's hand across the month. The early entries upright and tired and his, the loops closed the way Gin had closed them since he was a boy learning to write his name small enough to fit the school forms. Then, after the fourteenth, the drift. Every downstroke a single degree off true, steady, deliberate, almost graceful, as though a second person with very good penmanship had begun, gently, to correct him.

A shaking hand Rei could have grieved cleanly. This was worse. He did not need Kurosawa to read the body for him any more. He had read it in the cardigan, and in the way the thing said we, and in the two kinds of gladness in one face at the rail. The handwriting only made it a measurement.
And a measurement is a rate. That was the sum he had refused to do all month.
Gin had done that sum for other people. Rei found it in the back third of the book, in a section headed with the dry title Gin gave everything that frightened him.

doc.title: Gin's book. Partial possession. What the case files show
lines: Compiled from the Satō file and four others. Times vary. The shape does not.

Before. A patient entity can watch a practitioner for a year and a half and do nothing visible. It waits for one night when his real stability drops below the floor his suppression is pretending to hold. The suppression smooths over the very signal he would have used to notice. It may wait a week. It may wait two years.
The night. It takes approximately the time between two thoughts. In the files, the host often does one small ordinary thing at the last moment, as if part of him knew.

After. The entity runs the surface well. Messages in his voice. Work attended. Assessments read clean. The tells are tiny. One missed appointment he would never miss. One file pulled without reason. One joke that does not land.
Two weeks. It notices questions. People who ask begin to find his contacts harder to reach.
Four weeks. The critical point. Without a recovery team being built, consolidation speeds up. His surfaces get shorter.
Six weeks. Ejection risk. His own consciousness begins to be pushed out. Reaching him now needs work at the Threshold.
Eight weeks. The window closes. Full possession. Without Threshold transit, ejection cannot be undone. What remains of him is what he wrote down.
It speeds up when someone makes loud direct contact, when a practitioner near it breaks his own suppression where it can see, when watched contacts are burned. Each costs days.
It slows when someone reaches him in a surface, even briefly. When someone learns the entity's history. When someone builds a team able to do the exorcism. Each buys days.
The clock is never announced. It is felt.

blocks.p: One small ordinary thing at the last moment. Rei thought of the walkway outside the flat on the first night. Gin's keys lying on the concrete by the door, set down neatly, as if put there on purpose. The desk lamp still on. He had thought for a month that it meant Gin had been taken in a hurry. It meant the opposite. Gin had had just enough time to leave his brother a sign.
He counted the weeks from the Wednesday Gin went quiet. He counted them twice on his fingers like a child. More than four. Not yet six.

Then he made himself do the second sum, the one a person does about a parent in a ward, where the number is small and the units are unbearable. He went back through the month and found the days that had moved. The night he went through at the Senju node and came back with a stranger's tools in his hands, his suppression broken wide open in a ward the Healer watched. Days lost. The kitchen at two in the morning, when Gin surfaced long enough to say don't take it. Days bought. The phone call. The knock on the receiver. The embankment, and a cold hand held all the way home through Ōji while the knuckles pressed back, once, then once, then once. Days bought.

He let his registers up and read the page the way only he could, both sides at once, and the lean told him its rate. It was gaining. It was not finished. There was still a margin. Thin as the wall, soft as the ice, a hand's width of his brother not yet corrected.

The Healer knew it too. It had always known. It had been patient precisely because it was letting this clock run slow on purpose, keeping a little brother in reserve. A little brother was the lure that kept Rei coming to the river. An empty body was not. The cruellest clock was the one the Healer had its thumb on, slowing it, so the bait stayed fresh until the wall and the chair arrived.

He might have stopped there. He nearly did. But the lean was not even. On one page near the end, an entry about the weather and a broken heater, the corrections stopped looking like corrections. For six lines the second hand wrote by itself.

doc.title: Gin's book, an entry after the 14th. The second hand
lines: Subject's rank is presented as C and has been for six years. Real rank Vanguard, suppressed, held under repeated assessment, unnoticed.
Aperture strong. Multi-path. Works alone. No institutional welfare check would flag his stability falling.
Lives three hundred metres from the warm place and inside the range of the vacant thirteenth.
Line of Uedera. The development points toward the seat. Not his body. His access.
He does not know he is tired.

blocks.p: It was a clinical note. A doctor's note. Under it, at the foot of the page, the pen had begun a signature in old-fashioned characters, firm and practised, as though out of a habit of forty years. 橘 癒士郎. Then a single line had gone through it, almost gently.

Gin had written once, on the page about the thing in him, that it wrote truer than it meant to. Rei sat looking at the crossed-out name until the characters stopped being shapes. Tachibana. Yushiro. The second name meant something like healing man.
He rang Tanizaki. The old man answered on the fourth ring, which meant he had been sitting by the phone.
"I've got a name," Rei said, and read it out, and heard the silence on the other end go a different shape.

"The Grid's old books remember a doctor," Tanizaki said at last. His voice was thin on the line and very steady. "In this ward. Forty years ago or near it. There were people dying who would have been left, and he would not leave them. He stayed at it past the point a living man can. When he crossed, he crossed through Duty. The charge he would not put down. The books say afterwards he wanted no seat and no sensation. Only to finish."
"The CVD calls that register nothing," Rei said.

"The CVD calls a great many things nothing." A cup was set down somewhere. "Listen to me, boy. I have known your brother since he was smaller than you were when I met you. Most of them, you say the name and it's a blade. Not this kind. Said by someone the vessel loves, the name doesn't cut it. It holds it. Anchors it in place. Like a hand on a shoulder." A pause. "You understand what I'm telling you. It isn't a weapon. It's a leash, and only one person in this city can hold the end of it."
"And if I say it and it doesn't want to be held?"
"Then you'll have told a doctor his own name," Tanizaki said. "In my experience they don't hear it often."
After the call Rei went back to the section of the book Gin had marked only with a small drawing of a hook. He had read it once, weeks ago, and not understood it. Now he did.

doc.title: Gin's book. Family note
lines: Two Uedera ancestors were field operatives in the early years of veil work. Their case files show outcomes no single-path practitioner of their recorded rank could have managed. They never opened their paths on purpose. They held them shut and used them, now and then, under extreme pressure, without understanding what they were doing.

I recognised the pattern after my own exposure. The multi-path aperture seems to run in the family. So does the habit of hiding it. I taught Rei the suppression at the kitchen table as if it were a trick for sleeping. It is the only configuration I have ever drawn that was entirely an act of love.

If it is ever me inside something, there are two ways in. Clairsentience at the tenth level. Frequency Isolation. Finding one consciousness inside a possessed body, as one voice is found in a crowd. And if I am thrown out and not yet gone, Teleportation at the tenth level. Threshold Crossing. Reaching a soul that has been ejected but has not dissolved.
Rei will never have the second. He may have the first without knowing.
Some of the old ones have known about our line for longer than I have. I do not know which. I have felt one of them look at me as if remembering something.

blocks.p: As if remembering something. Rei thought of the face at the centre of the light, looking at him like a word it had lost. He turned the registry over and on the blank back of it he began to write, slowly, everything he knew about the man who held the empty chair.

Gin's page about the Account Book gave him most of it. Kasumi Shin, who held Awe and stood nearer the centre than any of the others, had once shown Gin a book older than the Accord. Gin had copied out one entry from its first pages because it had disturbed him. An investigator of the Edo period who served the Twilight Office, the old office of Ōmagatoki that looked into what came through at dusk. A man who would not take either side of any line and walked the middle way between them, until he had opened every path and every register at once and there was nothing left of him that was only one thing. Gin had copied the family name, Kuze, and then one character for the given name, 要, with a question beside it. Kaname? The rivet of a fan. The pin everything turns on.
Rei wrote it out in six lines and looked at them.

doc.title: The back of the registry page, in Rei's hand
lines: His name is Kuze Kaname.
He comes from the Edo period.
He served the Twilight Office.
He walked the middle way.
He was an investigator.
He became the Duty seat. He is still sitting in it.

blocks.p: He had been wrong about the chair all month. Everyone had. It was not empty. It had a man in it who had forgotten he was one.

blocks.cap: All three pages in sight at once, the lamp guttering, the festival drums starting up across the ward

blocks.p: Now he laid the three rates beside one another and let them be what they were. Three clocks that could not all reach the bottom of the hour together, because the bottom of the hour was one hour, the soft middle of the last night.

The wall would open tonight and shut at dawn. Fixed, honest, indifferent. The chair would borrow that hour and take whoever was closest when the ice went soft. Patient, conditional, hungry. And Gin was gaining toward the end of his eight weeks, not yet there, held open on purpose. Cruel, slowed, baited. Three needles dropping toward the same number at three speeds.
Under the whole month's dread, the clarity had been waiting for him all along. Whichever one resolved first would not only resolve itself. It would close the other two.

If dawn came and nothing had been pushed through, the wall would heal on its own schedule, the chair would go on asking, and Gin would be left at whatever degree he had reached. If the chair was filled while the ice was soft, the wall would be written on before dawn could heal it, and everything else would bend to whatever had sat. If the Healer's thumb slipped, or it decided the bait had done its work, and the last degree of Gin went over first, then there would be no brother to weigh against anything, and the night would only be about cost.

The drums started across the ward, the slow Obon rhythm the whole city has agreed means welcome home to the dead. Under Rei's half-raised registers the second light came up behind every sound the way it came up behind every lantern. He gathered the three pages and squared their edges. He did not pretend any more that he was reading them. He knew which clocks were gaining.
He had a name for the thing in his brother, and a name for the man in the chair, and a square of washi over his heart. It was not a plan. It was what Gin would have called a kit.
He went to the desk and opened the bottom drawer.
